svg.title: On the first run, the toolbox names the exact thing to fix: Every check stops and names the fix, and init finishes cleanly once GitLab is turned off
svg.text: On the first run, the toolbox names the exact thing to
Scenario: Every check stops and names the fix, and init finishes cleanly once GitLab is turned off
The check names what is missing, and the command that installs it
The check reads the right GitLab host
init names the exact fix, then bows out cleanly

g.text: Given a developer's project points at the company's own GitLab, with
none of the toolbox's tools installed yet
A copy of the toolbox on a fresh machine. Its git remote points at the company's own GitLab,
gitlab.selfhosted-corp.example.
The toolbox needs three tools: gum, glow and glab, the GitLab command line tool. None of them
is installed yet, and the shell answers "command not found" for each.
When the developer runs the GitLab check, it names the missing tool and
the setup that installs it
The developer runs the GitLab check. It stops at the first tool it misses: "Required UI
dependency missing: gum", and the run ends on "Failed to run task".
It names the command to run, task dev:setup-environment, the setup that installs every tool
the toolbox needs. Off camera, a machine that already has gum gets the same advice for glow,
and one that has both is told to install glab.
When the developer runs that setup, the check names the company's GitLab
host and offers to sign in
The developer runs task dev:setup-environment, then the check again. The setup installs every
tool, a long run that scrolls off the screen, so the card starts at its last line,
"Development environment setup completed successfully".
Nobody has signed in yet, so the check shows "GitLab Authentication Required". "Target Host:
gitlab.selfhosted-corp.example" is the host it read from the git remote. Below it, the check
asks "Continue and sign in now?", and waits for Yes or No.
Then an SSH-style gitlabssh remote still leads the check to the same GitLab host
The developer answered No, and now points the remote at the address the company's GitLab gives for SSH clones. git
remote -v shows git@gitlabssh.selfhosted-corp.example.
The check still says "Target Host: gitlab.selfhosted-corp.example". It turns the gitlabssh name back into the gitlab
one, the address where you sign in.

text.tspan: git remote set-url origin git@gitlabssh.selfhosted-corp.example:acme/widgets.git && git remote -v && task

g.text: Then a GitHub remote is refused, with the exact command to point it back at GitLab
Now the remote points at github.com. The check stops at once with "No GitLab repository remote was detected." It never
asks to sign in.
It prints the exact line that points the remote back at GitLab, git remote set-url origin
https://gitlab.com/<namespace>/<project>.git, and then task devsecops:init.

text.tspan: git remote set-url origin https://github.com/acme/widgets.git && git remote -v && task glab:auth:ensure

g.text: When the developer points the remote back at GitLab and runs init, it
stops at the sign-in and names the command to run
The developer follows that advice with gitlab.com and runs init. It first runs the same setup
again, which finds every tool already installed. The card starts at the last line of that
setup, "Development environment setup completed successfully".
Then init reaches its GitLab step and shows the same sign-in card, now for "Target Host:
gitlab.com". The developer answers No, and init pauses with the two commands to run, "task
glab:auth" and then "task devsecops:init".

text.tspan: git remote set-url origin https://gitlab.com/acme/widgets.git && task devsecops:init

g.text: Then a project that stays on GitHub turns the GitLab integration off, and init finishes
cleanly
A project that stays on GitHub has no GitLab to sign in to. It turns the GitLab part of the toolbox off with
TASK_GLAB_ENABLED=false and runs init on its GitHub remote.
Most of the card is init checking every tool again and finding each one already installed. Versions show as X.Y.Z. Then
init skips its GitLab step: the task runner says devsecops:init:configure "is up to date". It ends on "DevSecOps project
initialization completed", with no sign-in question and no refusal of the remote.

text.tspan: git remote set-url origin https://github.com/acme/widgets.git && TASK_GLAB_ENABLED=false task devsecops:init
